section_summary: This section covers documents from late 1941 to late 1943 concerning motion pictures and related visual media involving Japan. In late August and early September 1941, Ambassador Joseph C. Grew and Commercial Attaché Frank S. Williams report on the critical situation facing American motion picture distributors in Japan, whose Japanese employees demanded exorbitant retirement allowances and issued threats amidst impending Japanese film monopolies and frozen assets. Later wartime records from 1943 include a Tokyo Domei broadcast report on educational slide production by Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai for Southeast Asia, an Alien Property Custodian inquiry regarding vesting orders for Japanese government-owned films in the United States, Office of War Information correspondence attempting to locate the Japanese naval film 'Our Fleet' for a Pacific War documentary, and a cross-reference noting Finnish Foreign Office reactions to the Japanese film 'Japan's Wild Eagles'.

subfiles.about: Concluding page of a diplomatic despatch from Ambassador Grew urging State Department protection for American motion picture companies facing exorbitant severance demands in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Concluding page of Despatch 5824: Grew urges the U.S. government to recognize the plight of American film companies and protect them from exorbitant demands, enclosing Williams's memorandum and an oral statement.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5824 from Embassy Tokyo Regarding Protection of American Film Companies (Concluding Page)

subfiles.about: A memorandum detailing exorbitant retirement allowance demands, unauthorized meetings, and police threats made against eight American film companies in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Frank Williams reports all eight American film companies face Japanese staff demands for two years' salary plus three months per year of service, over a million yen, with unauthorized meetings, police threats and claims on 11.5 million yen of frozen profits; he urges representations.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Commercial Attaché Frank S. Williams on Demands Faced by American Motion Picture Companies in Japan

subfiles.about: An oral diplomatic statement lodged with the Japanese Foreign Office regarding exorbitant severance demands and threats directed at American motion picture distributors.
subfiles.summary: Grew's oral statement to Foreign Office bureau chief Terasaki protests severance demands over a million yen, rejection of standard terms, and office meetings with threats of police detention and exit bans, and asks Japan to protect the firms.
subfiles.title: Oral Statement Presented by Ambassador Grew to Foreign Office Bureau Chief Terasaki

subfiles.about: A monitored Domei news broadcast reporting on color picture slides produced by the Society for International Cultural Relations to promote Japanese life in southern regions.
subfiles.summary: Domei broadcast: the Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai has made two series of 100 color slides of Japanese life for southern regions, with projectors, including oil-lamp models for areas without electricity.
subfiles.title: Domei English Broadcast on Educational Slide Series by Kokusai Bunka Shinkokai

subfiles.about: A cross-reference file note concerning a proposed Vesting Order by the Alien Property Custodian for Japanese government-owned motion picture films in the United States.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Alien Property Custodian's June 5, 1943 letter on Japanese Government-owned films, enclosing a proposed Vesting Order and asking State's objections; file 740.00115 P.W. Japanese Government/1.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Proposed Vesting Order for Japanese Government-Owned Films

subfiles.about: A letter from the Office of War Information requesting a print of the Japanese propaganda film 'Our Fleet' for use in an American documentary about the Pacific War.
subfiles.summary: Philip Dunne of the Office of War Information asks John Begg whether State holds the two-reel Japanese film "Our Fleet," footage he needs for a Pacific War film, and whether a print can be provided.
subfiles.title: Letter from Philip Dunne to John Begg Requesting Japanese Film 'Our Fleet'

subfiles.about: A response from the State Department stating that it does not hold the Japanese film 'Our Fleet' and suggesting contact with the Navy Department.
subfiles.summary: Begg tells Dunne no State officers know of "Our Fleet" in their custody, suggests the Navy Department might have it, and hopes to meet in New York.
subfiles.title: Letter from John M. Begg to Philip Dunne Regarding Custody of Film 'Our Fleet'

subfiles.about: A cross-reference file note referencing a diplomatic despatch from Finland on the Finnish Foreign Office's stance toward the Japanese film 'Japan's Wild Eagles'.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: McClintock's Despatch 2673 (December 13, 1943) on the Finnish Foreign Office's attitude to the film "Japan's Wild Eagles," file 811.4061 Motion Pictures/1355.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Finnish Foreign Office Attitude Toward 'Japan's Wild Eagles'
